s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological disorder with autonomic dysfunction and cognitive decline
key_facts: 3-year history of progressive disorder
Denies paresthesias, dysesthesias, or loss of sensation
Abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function without orthostatic hypotension
Patchy decrease in sweat output on quantitative sudomotor axon reflex test
Near complete global anhidrosis on thermoregulatory sweat test
Low α-galactosidase activity (0.056 U/L)
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein levels (95 mg/dL)
No pleocytosis in cerebrospinal fluid
Bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami on MRI Brain
Global diffuse brain volume loss on MRI Brain
No spinal cord lesions on MRI Spine
Positive for pseudo-α-galactosidase allele
Mild neurocognitive and memory deficits on neuropsychological testing

shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological disorder with autonomic dysfunction and cognitive decline

shortlist.label: Fabry Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Low α-galactosidase activity and positive for pseudo-α-galactosidase allele

shortlist.label: Alpha-Galactosidase Deficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Low α-galactosidase activity and positive for pseudo-α-galactosidase allele

shortlist.label: Frontotemporal Dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Cognitive decline and progressive neurological disorder

raw.rationale: The patient's low α-galactosidase activity, positive pseudo-α-galactosidase allele, and symptoms such as autonomic dysfunction, generalized ataxia, and cognitive decline are consistent with Fabry Disease, a genetic disorder caused by deficiency of α-galactosidase A

rejected.label: Multiple System Atrophy
rejected.why: Lack of orthostatic hypotension and specific pattern of autonomic dysfunction

rejected.label: Alpha-Galactosidase Deficiency
rejected.why: Too broad, Fabry Disease is a specific type of alpha-galactosidase deficiency

rejected.label: Lewy Body Dementia
rejected.why: No mention of visual hallucinations, fluctuations in cognitive function, or REM sleep behavior disorder

rejected.label: Frontotemporal Dementia
rejected.why: No prominent frontal or temporal lobe symptoms, and lack of characteristic MRI findings
